decision.physicalSubstrate: a dedicated, typed, append-only SQLite file ($DSH_HOME/palimpsest/execution-associations.sqlite; the deployment may pass an explicit path)
decision.trustedWriteEntryPoint: createExecutionAssociationRecorder(...) — bound to the deployment's own TrustedSourceBasis and SourceKind, reachable only from the composition that wired the worker port
decision.readReplayBoundary: makeAssociationQualifier(...) — replays typed records, re-reads canonical Work, re-reads the real DSH Session header, and compares the record's basis to the verifier's own

SESSION_IDENTITY_OBSERVED.note: immutable facts only — NO ingestion timestamp, so a retry is byte-identical (§7.4)

failureModes: malformed payload → fail closed before any write, through ExecutionAssociationStoreError
same eventId with different content → ExecutionAssociationConflictError (no last-write-wins)
malformed stored record on replay → fail closed; never read as an empty history
observer/store failure → reported, never converted into a Work success or failure (§7.7)
decision.migrationCompatibility: a NEW dedicated file and a NEW concern; it adds no Work event type, no projector case and no snapshot table. Older readers are unaffected because nothing else reads this file.
decision.defaultCapabilityAbsenceBehavior: a deployment that does not compose the concern simply has no execution-association evidence. Work, Delegation and the Worker Port do not import it (verified: src/interaction/work_delegation.ts contains no `execution_association` reference), so ordinary Work execution is unchanged when the concern is absent (§7.7).

rejectedAlternatives.reason: §6.1: a Host observation is not a Work lifecycle transition. Writing it as a Work event would place an observation inside the canonical lifecycle and risk the invalid implication `session created ⇒ attempt progressed`. settleMutatingWork must remain the only thing that completes an attempt.

§6.2: its semantic ownership is peer coordination/federation (participation, collaboration, commitment, handoff), and it is composed only when a deployment wires the full federation surface. Reusing it would either merge concern domains under one authority or silently require a peer stack to record a purely local Host fact. Its idempotency/atomicity contract is retained as the REFERENCE this store is modelled on.
verifiedFacts: src/coordination/store.ts: the store is constructed by src/deployment/launch.ts:306 from profile.databases.coordination
src/composition/collaboration.ts: the participation/federation surface is composed only when localPeer + coordinationStore + peerTransportPort + peerDirectoryPort + attemptCatalog are all present

rejectedAlternatives.reason: §6.3: a research script. Its principles (controlled ingestion, content digest, atomic publication, conflict refusal, rejection of caller-declared origin markers) are reused, but it is not promoted into production architecture, and a self-computed digest is not independent provenance when the writer may choose both data and digest.

§6.4: selected. A source-grounded comparison showed the existing facilities cannot safely accommodate the concern (A: wrong authority; B: absent without federation). The store is small, typed, adds no runtime or scheduler, stores no DSH event bodies and no copy of canonical Work state.

precedent: src/project_world/basis_store.ts — a dedicated L2 append-only store owning its own file rather than an event-sourced Work table, for the same 'execution provenance is not Work state' reason. The P2-B store follows its design.
